hypoxia induces hyperpermeability of endothelial cells via the release of vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGFs) which in turn lead to the dislocalisation, decreased expression, increased phosphorylation of zonulae occludentes-1 and changes in the cytoskeleton.

hypoxia causes the release of VVEGF, which in turn causes the dislocalization of ZO- 1, decreased expression, enhanced phosphorylation of the ZO1 protein, and increased paracellular permeability in the BBB.
hypoxia leads to the disruption of the ZO1 expression and distribution, which correlates with an increased permeability in endothelial cells.

the development of new methods for the treatment of brain edema, the most frequent complication in the therapy of acute brain damage.
the role of VEGF and ZO-1 on the regulation of BBB permeability during hypoxia.
the mechanisms of the regulation of paracellular permeability in brain microvascular endothelial cell monlayers.

we found that the hypoxia-induced hyper permeability in brain microvascular endothelial cell monocytes is regulated by the vascular endothelial growth factors and the expression of the protein ZO-1.

hypoxia can induce the release of vascular endothelial growth factors from endothelial cells.
hypoxia induces the release of VVEGF, which in turn decreases the expression of ZO- 1, a protein that is involved in the formation of tight junctions.
